Callback enqueue, bypassing, segmentation, advancement and invocation paths.
Priority boosting trigger policy, thread main loop and interaction with scheduler.
Barrier entry, propagation and completion coordination.
Dynticks idle and watching transitions and tick handling.

findings.text: Tree combining node for grace coordination. It stores a local sequence view with furthest requested future sequence and quiescent completion tracking. Normal and expedited participation use staged masks with active, per period initial, and next period copies, plus offline capture, overload and functional masks. Topology uses parent link, low and high CPU bounds, group number, depth with root at zero, and single bit upward mask. Blocked readers queue with selectors for normal, expedited and boost need. Boost support adds timing, thread handle and status. Offload waiting, forcing lock, expedited lock with sequence and wait queues and poll lock with sequence and work complete the layout. Members include gp_seq, gp_seq_needed, completedqs, qsmask family, expmask family, cbovldmask, ffmask, grpmask, grplo, grphi, grpnum, level, parent, blkd_tasks, gp_tasks, exp_tasks, boost_tasks, boost_time, fqslock, exp_lock and exp_poll_lock.

Per CPU state split into quiescent handling, batching, idle tracking, barrier and expediting, offload, boosting and diagnostics. Quiescent handling keeps sequence views, no quiescent flags for normal and expedited kinds, online and wrap indicators, leaf link with upward mask, tick counts and deferred attention mechanisms. Batching uses a segmented callback list with overload and invocation accounting and a processing bound. Idle tracking keeps watching snapshots and urgency flags. Barrier and expediting keep sequence snapshots and watching checks. Offload when enabled adds sleep queues, thread handles, bypass and regular lists with timing and counting, and wake chain links with cacheline separation. Boosting adds per CPU thread state. Diagnostics add stall snapshots, irq work tracking, offline and online records and lazy length with CPU number. Members include gp_seq, cpu_no_qs, mynode, grpmask, cblist, blimit, watching_snap, barrier_seq_snap, nocb_bypass, nocb_gp_seq, snap_record, lazy_len and cpu.

Global grace controller with node hierarchy, CPU accounting, sequence management, barrier coordination, expedited coordination, timing and identity. Hierarchy is a fixed node array with per level index. Root guarded region holds current sequence, maximum duration, grace thread handle with wait queue, command flags, sleep state and wake timing plus polled snapshots. Barrier region uses a mutex, waiter count, completion and sequence with a separate spin guard for snapshots. Expedited region serializes entry and wakeup with ticket sequence, wait queue and overload indicators. Timing covers forcing, kicking, start and end, activity, stall checks and reschedule points. Identity is a name with abbreviated character. Offline synchronization, synchronize queue with wait nodes and cleanup work, and offload setup guard complete the layout. Members include node, level, ncpus, gp_seq, gp_kthread, gp_wq, gp_flags, gp_state, barrier_mutex, barrier_sequence, exp_mutex, expedited_sequence, jiffies_force_qs, jiffies_stall, name, abbr, ofl_lock, srs_next and srs_wait_nodes.

Small per CPU deficit carrier with two views. Byte view holds separate normal and expedited indicators. Halfword view provides their combined aggregate for single check. Stored inside per CPU data to record that no quiescent state has yet been observed for the current period of each kind. Members are norm, exp and the aggregate.

Diagnostic snapshot captured for stall analysis. It records sequence view, accumulated hard and soft interrupt time plus kernel task time, counts of hard and soft interrupts and context switches, and jiffies at capture. Stored per CPU for later comparison when a period appears stuck.

Fixed pool element for synchronize waiters. It pairs an atomic in use marker with an intrusive queue link, allowing a small bounded set of waiter headers to be linked into grace wait lists without allocation.

Root node lock guards global sequence and associated grace thread control including flags, sleep state and wake timing plus polled snapshots. Barrier mutex guards barrier count, completion and sequence while a dedicated spin guard protects per CPU barrier snapshots. Expedited entry and wakeup each have their own mutex with ticket sequence and wait queue. Offline versus pre initialization races use a dedicated arch spin guard. Thread spawn and affinity changes use a per node mutex.

Each tree node carries separate guards for forcing, expedited reporting and polled expedited requests, with the latter two including sequence request state and wait or work items. Boost uses a real time mutex only for its side effect, not as a lock. Offloaded CPUs add separate locks for GP thread, bypass enqueue and callback coordination, placed to reduce cache contention, with disabled interrupt acquisition for bypass attempts. Per CPU irq work pending state is guarded by the leaf node lock.

Normal grace participation uses three generations of masks. Next generation accumulates membership for the upcoming period, initial is loaded from it at period start, and active is cleared as quiescent states arrive. Leaf bits map to per CPU data while internal bits map to child nodes. A separate mask captures offline CPUs observed during initialization.

Expedited participation mirrors normal staging with active, initial and next copies. Next accumulates every CPU that has ever been online for future expedited periods. Active is tested before reporting and cleared on report, with rechecks under lock because concurrent completion can race with local handling.

Hierarchy is a tree with root depth zero increasing downward. Each node covers a contiguous CPU interval with low, high and group number for the level above. Upward reporting uses a single bit mask unique to the child position. Each per CPU record points at its leaf and carries the matching leaf bit.

Readers blocked inside read side sections queue on their leaf node with newer entries at one end aging toward the other. Three selectors identify the earliest task relevant to the current normal period, the current expedited period, and the earliest needing priority boost. A null selector means no such task exists, and boost need implies normal period blocking exists.

Sequence numbers increase monotonically across periods. Global, per node and per CPU views track the same counter, with per CPU and per node needed markers recording the furthest future request. Snapshot fields in diagnostic and barrier state record the sequence at specific events. Wrap risk is flagged per CPU with a counter of observed wraps.

Grace thread sleep state advances through idle with no period, waiting for start then start done, hotplug handling, initialization, waiting for forcing time then forcing done, cleanup started then cleanup done. Command flags request initialization, forcing and overload handling orthogonally to the sleep state.
Three command bits for the grace thread have values one for initialization need, two for forcing need and four for overload indication.
Deferred quiescent reporting uses zero for idle with nothing pending and one for pending scheduler or irq work attention.
Offload wake decisions use an ordered scale with zero meaning no wake, one for bypass list, two for lazy callbacks and three for full wake.

Forcing interval grows with timer frequency as one plus one if HZ exceeds two fifty plus one if HZ exceeds five hundred. Force divisor is two fifty six for very large systems. Stall ratelimit delay is two. Lazy flush delay is ten seconds worth of ticks with a mutable current threshold initialized to that value. Bypass allowance per tick scales as sixteen thousand divided by HZ.

Two build flavors select abbreviated and raw names. Preempt flavor uses p with rcu_preempt and sched flavor uses s with rcu_sched. One form exposes the raw name directly as a macro while the other keeps a mutable character buffer with a trace variable aliasing it and a macro pointing at the buffer.
Synchronize waiter pool bounds concurrent users woken from a period at five and bounds normal wait headers at five, matching the fixed wait node array size.
Work handler for expedited completion waiting. It recovers its enclosing expedited work item from the work handle and then invokes the selective wait wake path for the associated grace state.

Marks the current CPU as still needing an expedited quiescent state, ensuring the urgent flag becomes visible after the deficit flag, and requests rescheduling. Caller must run with interrupts disabled and hold exclusive write ownership of the deficit indicator.

Inter processor handlers for expedited quiescent forcing share a contract with two build variants. Both ignore CPUs no longer awaited or already marked. Idle or enabled contexts with no read side nesting report immediately, otherwise they defer. One variant inspects nesting depth and, when inside a read section, sets the deficit and a hint in the current task under node lock; negative depth warns. The other uses preemption and soft interrupt enablement plus idle interrupt origin to decide immediate versus deferred handling.

Work handler that drains a polled expedited request stored in its enclosing node. It claims the pending sequence under poll lock, returns if already completed, otherwise repeatedly requests expedited synchronization until the polled state observes completion, logging progress at bounded iteration counts, then marks completion under lock if the current request is satisfied.

Public polling helpers avoid unnecessary expedited waits. Conditional forms test the supplied old state or full sequence snapshot and only request an expedited period when not yet complete. The start helper captures a full snapshot then initiates a polled expedited request.

Boot time configuration for callback offloading. One option allocates the offload CPU mask, parses a CPU list when present with fallback to all CPUs on syntax error, and records setup completion. A second option enables polling mode for offload threads. The mask and poll flag persist as boot read state.

Bypass path uses a try lock that requires disabled interrupts. Flush attempts first verify list protection, offload status and successful try lock acquisition, then flush bypass entries with a warning if the flush reports failure.
Blocking wait helper that sleeps interruptibly and reschedules until a caller supplied condition becomes true, then restores running state before continuing.

Long grace periods risk missed quiescent reports, sequence wrap, callback overload and stalled CPUs. Mitigations include tick counts per period, force wake timing with call counts and start snapshots, per CPU reschedule and clock stamps, overload masks with global overload indicators, wrap flags with counters, and diagnostic snapshots of interrupt and switch activity for half timeout analysis.

Expedited handling faces lost wakeups and duplicate reports when completion races with interrupt arrival or read section exit. Defenses include rechecking active masks under lock after acquiring it, asserting exclusive write ownership of deficit flags, using release ordering between deficit and urgency flags, and separating expedited sequences, wait queues and poll state from normal grace state.
